The Mackinac Bridge connects the Upper and Lower peninsulas of the state of Michigan. It spans the Straits of Mackinac, a body of water connecting Lake Michigan and Lake Huron. Opened in 1957, the 26,372-foot-long bridge is the longest suspension bridge between anchorages in the Western Hemisphere.
